blocks.text: The customer journey covers acquisition (session 6), conversion (session 7) and retention (session 8). Acquisition generates money to meet costs and reinvest and shows traction to investors, partners and influencers – while acquisition costs have risen by over 50% in five years.

The acquisition funnel runs from awareness, interest, consideration and intent to evaluation and purchase; web analytics measures can be mapped to its stages. KPIs to compare campaigns or website versions: click-through rate, conversion rate, cost per sale and return on ad investment.
CAC = marketing costs / customers acquired, for a specific campaign or time window; include all marketing-related costs. How much you can spend depends on the customer's value (CLV, session 8).

A product is anything offered to satisfy a want or need – including services. Products have a core, tangible and augmented level; the product component model distinguishes physical, symbolic and service attributes plus legal conformity.
The new product development process: opportunity identification → design → testing → introduction → life cycle management, with GO/NO decisions at each step.
Customer value = benefits (functional, psychological, economic) − costs (monetary, perceived risk, inconvenience).
Measures of customer value (Lilien et al., 2017):
children: Objective: internal engineering assessment, indirect survey questions, value-in-use
Perceptual unconstrained: focus groups, direct survey questions, importance ratings
Behavioural: choice models (multinomial logit), data mining

blocks.text: Value-in-use is the maximum willingness to pay for a focal product given a reference. Compute the annual cost of the old solution (including downtime/shutdowns) and find the price at which the new solution costs the same.

Inferential statistics draws conclusions about a population from a sample. A test rejects or keeps H0 (no effect); type I error = rejecting a true H0 (α, usually 5%), type II error = keeping a false H0 (β).

A/B (split) testing compares a control (A) and a challenger (B) on a KPI – e.g. CTA colour or placement. Benefits: more traffic, higher conversion, lower bounce rate, lower cart abandonment. Use a t-test for metric KPIs (willingness to buy) and a chi-square test for categorical KPIs (choice).
The cost associated with bringing a new customer to the business, such as marketing costs, events and advertising, for a specific campaign or time window.
The part of a product that satisfies the customer's central underlying need or want.
Enhancements of the tangible product through additional services and features.
The maximum willingness to pay for a focal product, given a reference product (e.g. previous version, main competitor).
A marketing experiment that splits the audience to test variations of a campaign and determine which performs better.
Rejecting the null hypothesis although it is correct (α).
Not rejecting the null hypothesis although it is incorrect (β).
VIU appeared in every mock exam (chips, Z-rings). Always: annual old cost incl. shutdowns → equal to new cost → solve for price → compare with the offered price.
